available_definition: An instance is available at a measurement if Nova reports status ACTIVE and its SSH port (TCP 22) answers within 3 seconds. Otherwise it is unavailable.

measurement.method: Python program monitor.py using openstacksdk (Keystone authentication), Nova API for the status and a TCP connection to port 22 as network test
measurement.log_file: measurements.csv (date, instance, nova status, ip, ssh test, state)

formula: availability (%) = available measurements / total measurements x 100

tolerance_per_day.explanation: 288 x 0.5% = 1.44, so at most 1 failed measurement (1/288 gives 99.65%, 2/288 gives 99.31%). One failed measurement is about 5 minutes. The exact allowed downtime is 0.5% x 24 h = 7.2 minutes.

if_objective_not_met.99.0_to_below_99.5_percent: Provider sends an incident report within 24 h and grants a 10% service credit for the day
if_objective_not_met.below_99.0_percent: Provider sends an incident report within 24 h and grants a 25% service credit for the day
if_objective_not_met.repeated_failures: If the objective is missed 3 days in a row, the customer may ask for a review of the infrastructure

exclusions: Maintenance announced at least 24 hours in advance
Failures caused by the customer (stopping or deleting an instance on purpose, except for the controlled test below)
Failures of the customer's own network or the host machine

period.note: 2-hour test window, 24 measurements per instance, one every 5 minutes

controlled_outage.note: stopped then started with openstack server stop/start; detected as DOWN by monitor.py

monitoring_report.extension_to_one_day: A day has 288 measurements per instance; at most 1 failed measurement is tolerated (99.65%), 2 give 99.31%. The same 4 failures over a day would give 98.61%, still below 99.5%.
